children: Asian equity markets traded predominantly lower on Monday,

params.linkText: reversing early-session tailwinds from Wall Street

children: as geopolitical friction and surging energy prices weighed on risk sentiment.

U.S. equity futures came under immediate pressure following President Donald Trump’s rejection of an Iranian peace proposal aimed at ending Middle East hostilities and securing the Strait of Hormuz. In early trading, Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 0.76%, S&P 500 futures fell 0.39%, and Dow Jones futures slipped 0.42%.
In commodities, WTI crude oil climbed above $93 per barrel, while spot gold fell to around $4,200 an ounce.
South Korea’s KOSPI fell 2.55% to around 6,950, reversing gains from the previous session. The South Korean won traded around 1,358 per dollar, holding onto gains from the previous session.
